fact_text: A third-country professional cannot work in Cyprus on a generic status: to be employed by a company of foreign interests they must hold a temporary residence and employment permit issued for that specific purpose. The permit is not free-standing work authorisation; it is bound to the sponsoring company.
evidence_quote: In order for a third-party national to be employed in a company of foreign interests in the Republic, he must be a holder of a temporary residence and employment permit for this purpose

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a Cyprus job offer plus an entry visa is enough to start work. Actually a third-country national must hold a temporary residence AND employment permit issued for that purpose, tied to the sponsoring company. Action: confirm the employer lodges the permit application before you rely on starting work.

entity_title: No quota / no labour-market check for highly paid TCNs
fact_text: Under the Strategy in force since 2.1.2022, maximum quotas for foreign staff at companies of foreign interests are abolished, and such companies may employ any number of highly paid third-country nationals without a labour-market check. This removes the availability-of-local-workers test that normally gates third-country hiring.
evidence_quote: Maximum quotas for foreign staff are cancelled. Companies can freely employ any number of highly paid third-country nationals without going through a labour market check.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every non-EU hire must pass a labour-market test proving no local/EU worker is available. Actually highly paid hires at a registered company of foreign interests skip the quota and the labour-market check entirely. Action: confirm the role is classified 'highly paid' so the fast lane applies.

fact_text: Companies of foreign interests may staff up to about 70% of their workforce with third-country nationals: they commit to invest 30% of total staff in Cypriot/EU citizens over five years, and from 2.1.2027 the 70:30 ratio for new hires is checked, with any shortfall decided case-by-case by management.
evidence_quote: all companies commit to invest 30% of their total staff in Cypriots/EU citizens over a period of five years

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a foreign-interest company can hire unlimited non-EU staff indefinitely with no local-hire condition. Actually a 70:30 third-country-to-Cypriot/EU ratio applies and is checked on new hires from 2.1.2027. Action: ask HR whether the company is tracking the 30% local-hire commitment that underpins the permit route.

fact_text: To qualify as 'highly paid' employment at a company of foreign interests — the category that unlocks the fast-track permit, unlimited stay and easy change of employer — a third-country national must receive a minimum gross monthly salary of €2500. Legacy BCS Key Personnel on €2000+ may renew at the same employer until 31.12.2026 without raising pay.
evidence_quote: Receiving a minimum gross monthly salary of €2500

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any salaried offer qualifies for the foreign-interest fast track. Actually the 'highly paid' category requires a minimum gross monthly salary of €2500. Action: check the offer's gross monthly figure is at least €2500 before relying on the highly-paid route.

fact_text: The permit requires an employment contract of at least two years' duration. Even where only a one-year permit is sought, the contract must still run for — and carry stamp duties for — two years.
evidence_quote: Even if the application is submitted for a one-year permit, the contract must have a duration and corresponding stamp duties for 2 years.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a one-year permit only needs a one-year contract. Actually the contract must be for two years, with two years' stamp duty, even when applying for a one-year permit. Action: have the employer issue a 2-year contract and pay the 2-year stamp duty at the Tax Department.

entity_title: Employer must be on the Register of Foreign Interest Companies
fact_text: The fast-track permit route exists only if the employer is on the Register of Foreign Interest Companies. A company not already registered must first register at the Business Support Center (BSC) run by the Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, which confirms eligibility before the Migration Department will issue residence and employment permits.
evidence_quote: Businesses that are not already registered at the Register of Foreign Interest Companies of the Migration Department, should first register at the Business Support Center (BSC)

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employee applies for the fast-track permit directly. Actually the route depends on the employer first being registered as a company of foreign interests via the BSC. Action: confirm your employer holds Register of Foreign Interest Companies / BSC confirmation before counting on the fast track.

entity_title: Support-level hires still need a labour-market test
fact_text: The no-check fast lane is only for highly paid staff. For employment at the supportive level, a labour-market test and a contract sealed by the Department of Labour are required — the same gate highly paid hires are exempt from.
evidence_quote: A labour market test and a sealed contract by the Department of Labour are necessary

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed all staff at a foreign-interest company skip the labour-market test. Actually only highly paid staff are exempt; supportive-level roles still need a labour-market test and a Department of Labour-sealed contract. Action: if the role is below the highly-paid salary line, budget time for the labour-market test.

fact_text: Applications for residence and employment at companies of foreign interests are examined within one month, provided the file is complete. Incomplete applications fall outside the one-month commitment and take longer.
evidence_quote: The examination time of applications for residence and employment is set at one month

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed Cyprus work-permit processing takes many months. Actually a complete foreign-interest application is examined within one month. Action: submit a fully complete file — the one-month clock does not apply to incomplete applications.

fact_text: After arriving in Cyprus, the third-country national must register in the Aliens' Register and obtain the temporary residence and employment permit; first-time registration in the Aliens' Register carries a €70 fee. This produces the Alien Registration number/certificate (ARC) that identifies the person in the system.
evidence_quote: the third country national is required to register in the Aliens’ Register and obtain a temporary residence and employment permit

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the entry visa/permit is the only registration needed. Actually, after arrival you must register in the Aliens' Register (a €70 first-registration fee) to be issued your residence permit and Alien Registration number. Action: budget the €70 Aliens' Register fee and register promptly after arrival.

entity_title: Biometrics at the Cyprus Police immigration unit
fact_text: Issuing the temporary residence and employment permit requires the third-country national to give biometric data (photo and fingerprints) and a signature. Biometrics are captured at the District Immigration Unit of the Cyprus Police for the district of residence — not the Migration Department — and are needed again at each renewal.
evidence_quote: it is necessary the third country national to provide their biometric data (photo and fingerprints) and signature

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed all permit steps happen at the Migration Department in Nicosia. Actually biometrics (photo + fingerprints) are taken at your district's Cyprus Police Immigration Unit, and again at every renewal. Action: locate your District Immigration Unit and book the biometrics appointment.

entity_title: No maximum stay for highly paid TCNs
fact_text: A highly paid third-country national at a company of foreign interests may reside in Cyprus without any time limit, as long as they hold a valid temporary residence and employment permit. Support staff remain subject to the ordinary maximum-stay restrictions for third-country employment.
evidence_quote: as highly paid may reside in the Republic without a time limit, provided that they hold a valid temporary residence and employment permit

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed third-country work permits in Cyprus carry a hard maximum-stay cap. Actually highly paid staff at a foreign-interest company face no time limit while the permit stays valid; only support staff are capped. Action: keep the permit continuously valid to preserve unlimited-stay status.

fact_text: A highly paid employee may move to another company of foreign interests regardless of length of stay, provided they find new employment within one month of their previous employment ending and the new employer is also a company of foreign interests.
evidence_quote: finds employment within one month of the termination of his previous employment

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed an employer-tied permit means restarting the whole process to switch jobs. Actually a highly paid worker can change to another foreign-interest company if they re-employ within one month of the old job ending. Action: line up the next foreign-interest role inside the one-month window to keep permit continuity.
